items.title_orig: Pearl Jam issue statement condemning ICE arrests in Seattle
items.article_text:
Pearl Jam are the latest musicians to condemn the controversial Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Seattle legends Pearl Jam have issued a statement decrying the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement activity that saw officers detain a father and daughter on a jet bridge at the city's airport on Saturday. Footage of the incident swiftly went viral, prompting protests and stinging criticism from Pearl Jam.

"It is heartbreaking and infuriating to watch the human toll of a system driven by cold cruelty," say the band. "Seeing a family torn apart and dragged off a jetway right here in our own airport by masked individuals is unconscionable, and we stand firmly against this kind of inhumane treatment.

"That’s why this election mattered so much. It showed we aren't powerless or screaming into a void. Americans stood up, looked at the systematic abuse and what ICE is doing to our neighbours, and said, no more."

According to reports, ICE agents detained Mexican nationals Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and his daughter, Sofia Larrondo Hernandez Mejia, as they were boarding an Alaska Airlines flight from Seattle to Los Angeles. The pair were travelling to California to attend a family baptism, and are currently being held at an ICE processing centre in Tacoma, Washington.

Eddie Vedder & Co. aren't the first musicians to speak out against ICE. Paramore's Hayley Williams sparked a public back-and-forth with the Department of Homeland Security after shouting "Fuck ICE" during a show in Chula Vista, California, and Bruce Springsteen released the protest track Streets of Minneapolis, sparked by the deaths of US citizens Alex Pretti and Renee Good during protests against the organisation.

In January, Rage Against The Machine man Tom Morello organised an anti-ICE benefit concert at First Avenue in Minneapolis, and in July he released the protest song Pretend You Remember Me, in partnership with the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights of Los Angeles (CHIRLA), a nonprofit organisation that advocates for the city's immigrant community.

“This song is written for all the families torn apart by the recent immigrant purges and kidnappings," said Morello. "Children torn from their wailing mothers’ arms by masked government thugs, people coming home to find their loved ones abducted by the state. Folks who worked, suffered, and struggled for decades just to make a decent life for themselves and their family were violently separated with an uncertain future.

The latest news, features and interviews direct to your inbox, from the global home of alternative music.

"Pretend You Remember Me is for them and for all those who are finding the courage to stand up against racism, tyranny, and injustice."

A post shared by Pearl Jam (@pearljam)

items.title_orig: Pearl Jam Rage Against ‘Unconscionable’ ICE Arrests at Seattle Airport
items.article_text:
Pearl Jam called out ICE agents for their “inhumane treatment” of two people arrested at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport over the weekend.

Videos of masked ICE agents arresting Sofia Hernandez Meija and her father, Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza, have gone viral and sparked protests in Pearl Jam’s hometown of Seattle. Sharing an image of demonstrators, the band wrote, “It is heartbreaking and infuriating to watch the human toll of a system driven by cold cruelty. Seeing a family torn apart and dragged off a jetway right here in our own airport by masked individuals is unconscionable and we stand firmly against this kind of inhumane treatment.”

Meija and Mendoza were arrested Saturday, Nov. 21, on a jet bridge while trying to board a flight to Los Angeles, where they were traveling for a baptism. Videos showed ICE agents struggling with a man on the ground and trying to drag him out while other passengers filmed and photographed the incident. There were also videos of a woman being detained and carried out by agents as she cried out, sobbed, and, at one point, stated, “We have a work permit!”

In a statement, ICE accused Mendoza of being an undocumented immigrant from Mexico who “overstayed his visa.” They accused Meija of the same, while also claiming she obstructed the arrest and threw hot coffee at an agent. ICE said it plans to charge Meija with assaulting a federal officer.

Speaking with The Seattle Times, a lawyer for Mendoza and Meija, Olia Catala, said the two had been living in the United States since 2015 and were seeking asylum. Catala added that neither had a criminal record, and that Meija, who is married to a U.S. citizen, recently filed to change her citizenship status. The lawyer rebuffed ICE’s claim that Meija “hurled” a cup of coffee at an agent, saying, “When somebody’s charging at you, you’re going to drop a cup of coffee.”

After video of the arrests went viral, protests erupted in Seattle, including some demonstrations at the airport. In backing the protesters, Pearl Jam also pointed to the recent midterm and why the election “mattered so much.”

“It showed we aren’t powerless or screaming into a void,” the band wrote. “Americans stood up, looked at the systematic abuse and what ICE is doing to our neighbors, and said, no more.”
